mizutani: Pāṭaliputra: ruins between Patna and Dinapore (NW of Patna)
proposed: Patna: the Mauryan city between Bankipore and Patna City (Kumrahar, Bulandi Bagh, Panch Pahari)
basis: Spooner AR 1912-13 p. 24, EC 1913-14 p. 46 (Kumrahar hall, 8 x 10 columns), EC 1914-15 pp. 48-49 (Bulandi Bagh timber); Ghosh/Page AR 1926-27 pp. 135-136 (palisade 450 ft, "within the limits of the ancient city"); Chandra AR 1935-36 pp. 54-55 (Gonsai Khanda); fits Mizutani if his "Patna" = Patna City (he cites the palisade and hall); not W of Bankipore

name_zh: 八萬四千塔 (無憂王堵波)
proposed: unidentified; candidate Panch-Pahari mound C (Cunningham); Mauryan stūpas excavated in the same group at Bara Pahari
basis: Cunningham ASR XI p. 157: mound C from Faxian's 3 li S; Marshall AR 1915-16 pp. 11-14, Spooner EC 1915-16 pp. 30-34: two Mauryan stūpas in Bara Pahari (mound F), assigned to the five stūpas, not to this one; mound C not dug

proposed: unlocated; Waddell's Kumrahar fragments are columns of the Mauryan hall
basis: Spooner AR 1912-13 p. 24: fragments "could not all have formed part of a single pillar", hall of 8 x 10 columns; Cunningham ASR XI p. 159 spot G, nothing found; Agam Kuan (Page AR 1925-26 p. 31) concerns the hell, not this pillar

mizutani: no modern identification (SE of old Pāṭaliputra)
proposed: unidentified (near Pāṭaliputra)
basis: Beglar ASR VIII p. 27: unnamed small brick mound SE of Patna, no evidence; Cunningham ASR XI p. 162: not found; Beal, Dey give no site; gazetteers silent

proposed: unidentified
basis: no authority, gazetteer or survey report gives a site

proposed: Tillara (Bulandi mound W of the village)
basis: Beglar ASR VIII p. 33: Sangin Masjid jamb inscription naming Teladaka (read by Cunningham); Cunningham ASR VIII pref., XI pp. 162-166 (distances reconciled, Bulandi mound measured); Patna 1907: Pāla inscription naming Tailadhaka

proposed: Barābar Hill
basis: Beglar ASR VIII p. 36 (route followed without correction), adopted by Cunningham ASR XI p. 162, XV p. iv, XVI pp. 39-40, abandoning his 1871 site NW of Wazirganj; Pravara-giri-guhā named in the Barābar cave inscription (ASR I)

proposed: Dharawat (Kunwa Hill), Jahanabad subdivision
basis: Beglar ASR VIII pp. 36-39; Cunningham ASR XV p. iv, XVI pp. v, 45-46: monastery with back wall against the hill, summit stūpa of stūpa-stamped bricks with Gupta seals "Tathāgatasya Buddhasya", Kunwa < Guṇamati; Majumdar, Dey; Gaya 1906/1957 echo

proposed: Kauwa-dol hill
basis: Beglar ASR VIII pp. 39-40 (20 li SW on the ground; temple, colossal Buddha, creed inscription; 12 mi on to Gayā fits); Cunningham ASR XVI pp. 46-49 concurs, drops his Bithawa; stūpa-shaped peak, granite pillars; Dey; Gaya 1906/1957 echo

mizutani: Mora hill, c. 3 mi NE of Bodh Gayā
proposed: Mora range; cave on NW slope of Dhongra Hill
basis: Cunningham Mora Pahar; Gaya 1906/1957 (Oldham): cave with Buddhist image, terrace, seven stūpa remains on summit, distance 14-15 li

proposed: Bodh Gayā precinct; Xuanzang's enclosure a brick wall (untraced), not the stone railing
basis: Bloch AR 1908-09 pp. 143-147: railing inscriptions (Indrāgnimitra, Brahmamitra) date it to mid-2nd c. B.C., not Aśokan; railing originally round the Bodhi tree; Xuanzang's walls "built of bricks" (Bharhut relief); against Gaya 1906 pillar-height argument; precinct itself undisputed

proposed: the Mahābodhi temple
basis: Cunningham ASR I, III, XI p. 145 (theodolite height 160 ft vs 160-170; base vs 20 paces; E rooms later); Bloch AR 1908-09 p. 155: 6th-7th c. inscription on renewal of the same prāsāda; Spooner EC 1913-14 p. 71: Kumrahar plaque depicting the temple; Watters objects; Gaya 1906 echoes

proposed: open: Teskar Tal (Cunningham), Urel tank (Xuanzang's E bearing), or Muchharin
basis: Cunningham ASR I p. 10 Buchhokar Tal, then ASR XI p. 147 Teskar Tal reading W for E (pl. XL: C = Muchilinda's tank, D Urel Tal = Uruvilvā tank); Gaya 1906/1957: cult at Muchharin

proposed: unidentified
basis: no authority, gazetteer or survey report gives a site

mizutani: the great monastery mound N of the Mahābodhi temple (Cunningham map)
proposed: under the high plateau N and W of the temple
basis: Bloch AR 1908-09 p. 155: 6th-7th c. inscription names the monastery; remains "buried beneath the high plateau" N and W, unexcavated; Gaya 1957: extensive mound (Amar Simha's fort)

proposed: unidentified
basis: Cunningham ASR I p. 13 describes only the Bakror pillar; depends on 09.01.03

proposed: Mohana river
basis: Cunningham, Beal, Vivien, Dey unanimous; gazetteers incidental

name_zh: 屈屈吒播陀山 (窶盧播陀山)
proposed: Hasra Hill (Sobhnath) or Gurpa Hill
basis: Cunningham himself moves from three hills 1/2 mi N (ASR I) to Murali 3 mi NNE (ASR XV), still argued from the name; Gaya 1906/1957: Stein's Hasra (bearings, summit stūpa) conclusive vs Kurkihar; Banerji's Gurpa (Gurupāda, cleft, three peaks) favoured by Majumdar, Dey; Page AR 1922-23 p. 193 reports Sobnath as identified, no evidence

proposed: unidentified
basis: Cunningham ASR III pp. 139-140 Budhain: no stūpa or cave found; rejected by Majumdar (Stein, Jeshtiban position)

proposed: Tapoban hot springs
basis: Cunningham 1871, ASR III; Beal, Watters; Gaya 1906/1957 (Stein): two main springs with stūpa mound, 2 mi SW of Jethian

name_zh: 小孤山 (石室・阿素洛宮)
proposed: Asura palace = Rajpind cave, Chandu hill
basis: Gaya 1906/1957 (Stein): large cave with deep fissure, ancient walled road from Khiri; Beglar ASR VIII pp. 84, 89 had not found it

name_zh: 矩奢掲羅補羅城 (上茅宮城)
mizutani: Old Rājagṛha (Girivraja) in the hill-girt valley
proposed: Old Rājagṛha; outer walls on the hills = Xuanzang's 150 li unemended
basis: Marshall AR 1905-06 pp. 86-88: walls traced over all the hills to Giriak agree "remarkably well with the 150 li", Cunningham's 50-li emendation (ASR I) rejected; Page AR 1924-25 p. 38 repeats; Cunningham ASR I, III wall measurements

proposed: Chhatha-giri, with the Bimbisāra road and its two stūpas
basis: Marshall AR 1905-06 pp. 90-93: Chhatha-giri (after Broadley), not Saila-giri; causeway = Bimbisāra's road with the two stūpas "still there", opened; brick vihāra on W precipice; Kuraishi AR 1930-34 caves cleared, Buddhist seals; Nazim AR 1936-37 p. 47 two road stūpas and summit shrine cleared; Patna 1907 (Sen); Beglar ASR VIII Note (same peak, doubted the road)

mizutani: Ānanda cave, hole through the rock and bird marks extant on Gṛdhrakūṭa (Takakusu)
proposed: summit brick shrine (vihāra) and caves below it on Chhatha-giri
basis: Marshall AR 1905-06 pp. 92-93 ruined brick vihāra on W precipice (denies caves); Kuraishi AR 1930-34 caves, seals, Buddha; Chandra AR 1934-35 p. 17 small cave 30 ft below the shrine; Nazim AR 1936-37 p. 47 summit shrine, Eight-Buddha sealings, shrines E and S of the caves; which cave is Ānanda's not fixed

mizutani: Vipula hill, E of the exit from the N gate (Xuanzang's "west" read as "east")
proposed: Vipula hill E of the N gate, with the summit stūpa
basis: Cunningham 1871, ASR I (summit stūpa); Marshall AR 1905-06 p. 91 (northern mountain); Chanda AR 1925-26 pp. 122-123: old summit stūpa "evidently the one" Xuanzang saw; Chakravarti AR 1930-34: Kushan "parvato Vipula" inscription from Maniyar Math (not on the hill); Beal notes Baibhār fits the bearing

mizutani: cave on N face of Vaibhāra (Takakusu)
proposed: stone house at Jarasandh-ki-baithak with the Asura cave behind it, N face of Vaibhāra, W of the hot springs
basis: Cunningham ASR III pp. 140-142 found and cleared the cave; Beglar ASR VIII p. 89 accepts; Marshall AR 1905-06 pp. 93, 99-100 "no question" about the stone house and Asura cave W of the springs, a built structure; Page AR 1924-25 p. 38 tower

mizutani: = Faxian's 調達石窟, 3 li E of old N gate
proposed: cave M on the slope of Vipula
basis: Beglar ASR VIII p. 90: cave M on Cunningham's plan (ASR III pl. 41), in Mizutani's position; no description

mizutani: Veṇuvana outside the old city's N gate (flat site with memorial)
proposed: gardens 1 li N of the outer N gate, W of the road; vihāra under the mound with a Muslim saint's grave
basis: Marshall AR 1905-06 pp. 93-96: outer N gate moved to the Vaibhāra-Vipula defile; Bloch's trenches: nine brick stūpas on a concrete floor, 10th-11th c. creed tablets, Bodhisattva with ye dharmā; no inscription naming the garden

name_zh: 阿闍多設咄路王舍利塔
mizutani: mound E of the road, now Muslim cemetery (Takakusu)
proposed: E of the Veṇuvana: Takakusu's mound E of the road or Marshall's plinth at the foot of Vipula behind the Sūraj Kuṇḍ
basis: Marshall AR 1905-06 p. 96: plinth 12 ft high, W side 45 ft, 270 yd E of the garden, "possible", not dug; Faxian puts the stūpa W of the new city; Takakusu's mound also undug

proposed: Saptaparṇī hall on the levelled spur on the N face of Vaibhāra, c. 1 mile W of the Pippala house (Marshall); not Son Bhandar
basis: Marshall AR 1905-06 pp. 97-100: artificially levelled spur with ramps, cyclopean walls, pebble-paved forecourt at the 5-6 li; rejects Son Bhandar (S face, Jaina inscription), Beglar's fissures (not refound), Stein's Adinātha caves (ledge too narrow); a hall, not a cave; Beglar ASR VIII; Patna 1907

proposed: unidentified
basis: no authority, gazetteer or survey report gives a site

mizutani: pond 200 paces from Veṇuvana, locally Manavasar (test-excavated)
proposed: deep ancient tank N of the Veṇuvana mound
basis: Marshall AR 1905-06 pp. 95-96: "every reason to identify with the Karanda-hrada", no other tank; identity with the Manavasar not stated

name_zh: 無憂王堵波・石柱 (迦蘭陀池西北)
proposed: SW of New Rājagṛha: Cunningham's mound H (Takakusu's area)
basis: Cunningham ASR I pp. 24-25 robbed circular mound outside SW corner, no pillar; Marshall AR 1905-06 pp. 96-97 trenched mound H: Mauryan bricks reused over a medieval Jaina statue, earlier building "highly probable" on the site; 8th-9th c. clay stūpas

proposed: Nālandā ruins at Bargaon
basis: Cunningham ASR I pp. 28-35; Spooner EC 1916-17 pp. 43-46, AR 1916-17 pp. 16, 21: Śrī-Nālandā-mahāvihāra sealings at Site 1; Devapāla copper plate in Monastery 1 (AR 1920-21 p. 27; AR 1924-25 p. 117); Bāladitya temple inscription (AR 1925-26 pp. 131, 149); Harsha plaque (EC 1917-18 p. 44); Page AR 1926-27 plan

name_zh: 精舍 (如來三月說法處, 那爛陀伽藍西)
mizutani: probably the Mūlagandhakuṭī among caityas W of the monasteries
proposed: in the W range of stūpas and temples; Site No. 3 (Cunningham's A) disputed
basis: Cunningham ASR I pp. 29-30 mound A; Spooner (Patna 1907): Site 3 = three-month shrine; Hirananda Sastri EC 1919-20 p. 36: Site 3 = hair-and-nails stūpa S of the Avalokiteśvara image; Page AR 1926-27 W range of stūpas; Mizutani's area confirmed, mound open

proposed: unidentified (Cunningham: mound near Jagdispur, unconfirmed)
basis: Cunningham ASR I pp. 28-29: mound with large Buddha sculpture, from bearing and distance only; gazetteers silent

proposed: same, no site
basis: Watters, Beal agree on Nāla; Cunningham (1871, ASR I), Dey only c. 4 mi SE of Nālandā

proposed: Giriyek hill; cave = Gidhadwar
basis: Cunningham ASR I (goose figure and seals by the single stūpa), III pp. 144-150 (Haṃsa monastery terrace, route), XI; Beglar ASR VIII p. 78 cave; Patna 1907 echoes; Faxian equation conceded by Cunningham ASR XV p. 7

proposed: Parbati (Daryapur Parvati, "Ghar Pārāvat")
basis: Beglar ASR VIII pp. 108-113; Cunningham ASR XV pp. 4-10 final view (NE bearing, Pigeon's House name, terraced hill S of village, stūpa bricks E of monastery mound, Gupta monastic seal "saṅghasa") after ASR XI's Bihār/Soh-sarai; both need the emendation

proposed: Parbati hill, site A (dargah of Haji Chandar)
basis: Cunningham ASR XV pp. 8-9 (temple at centre of hill, now the dargah; Beglar's cells) after ASR XI p. 189 Bihār hill; follows 09.03.13; Gaya 1906/1957 echo

name_zh: 一伽藍 (孤山東南四十餘里)
proposed: unidentified (Aphsar if Kapotaka = Parbati; Tetrawa if Bihār)
basis: Cunningham ASR XI pp. 184-189 Tetrawa (inscriptions naming Tentaḍi-grāma) from Bihār; ASR XV pp. 10-11 Aphsar reading 4 li, nothing at 40 li; Gaya 1906 "doubt" repeats Cunningham's caveat

proposed: Shekhpura
basis: Cunningham ASR XV pp. 12-13 (bearing, distance, wooded route), revising 1871 Daryapur; Beal; Monghyr 1909/1960 echo; no remains

proposed: Rajjana (Rajaona), 2 mi NW of Lakhisarai
basis: Cunningham ASR XV pp. 12-15 (Balguzar Jhil = lake N of stūpa, statues in N mounds, onward distance to Monghyr), revising 1871 Rohinila; Dey, Beal report; Monghyr 1909/1960 echo
